prerequisites: It is recommended to have passed the course 'Organización y Gestión de Proyectos' (Project Organization and Management).

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire knowledge and abilities to organize and manage projects, including understanding the organizational structure and functions of a project office.

Be capable of drafting, signing, and developing projects in the field of Mechanical Industrial Engineering concerning the construction, renovation, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly, or operation of structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical and electronic installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing and automation processes.

Be capable of directing activities related to engineering projects: construction, renovation, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly, or operation of structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical and electronic installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing and automation processes.

Be capable of solving problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and of communicating and transmitting knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Mechanical Industrial Engineering.
Acquire knowledge for performing measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert opinions, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Be capable of handling specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Be capable of analyzing and evaluating the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Be capable of working in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Acquire knowledge, understanding, and capacity to apply necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Acquire the ability to draft Industrial Engineering projects and to direct activities specific to industrial engineering.
Possess abilities to solve problems with initiative and critical reasoning.
Acquire knowledge for performing measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert opinions, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Know how to handle mandatory regulations and standards.
Know how to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer, as well as the organizational structure and functions of a project office.

teaching_methods: Theoretical classes (lectures) with active-participative methodology, dialogues, and debates, supported by TIC tools (presentations, audiovisuals, documents).
Practical exercises in the classroom (cooperative work in teams using TIC tools).
Practical classes in the graphic expression laboratory using specific software for engineering projects and TIC tools, following PoPBL methodology (Problem-Project-Based Learning).
Support via telematic means, including AI tools for certain training activities.
assessment_rules: Continuous assessment is the default; students must explicitly opt for single assessment. To follow continuous assessment, 80% attendance to in-person activities is required. For passing, short answer tests require 70% correct answers, while problem-development tests, practical works (average of all practices), and the final project each require at least 5.0 out of 10. Non-delivery of all practical works or the project leads to failing the course. If a student fails any part, the final grade will be the weighted sum of passed components, but if this sum is 5 or more, the grade will be 4.9 (fail); if the exam is passed but practices/project are not delivered, the grade will be 4.0 (fail). Passed scores (>=5) for practical works and projects are saved for the current and potentially next academic year. Exam scores are not saved between calls. For the second call, there will be a single exam covering the entire course.
